primary.title: News Ltd. Planned a 40% Stake in the News of the World After a Pergamon Bid
primary.description_short: A 1968 Guardian report described a planned News Ltd. stake in the News of the World after a Pergamon Press takeover bid.
primary.description_medium: The Guardian reported on October 25, 1968 that News Ltd. planned to take a 40 per cent stake in the News of the World after Pergamon Press, led by Robert Maxwell, made a takeover bid. The report said Rupert Murdoch was to become joint managing director with Sir William Carr. It does not mention Donald Trump or establish a connection to him.
primary.description_long: The Guardian's archive report, published Friday, October 25, 1968, described an arrangement under which News Ltd. was to take a 40 per cent stake in the News of the World after a takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell, was defeated. The report said Rupert Murdoch, then chairman of News Ltd., was to become joint managing director with the newspaper's existing chairman, Sir William Carr. Its wording that the deal was unfolded the previous day places the report of the arrangement on October 24, although the archive item itself is dated October 25. The article describes a British newspaper ownership and management transaction; it does not report a Trump action or relationship. The frozen record's title and synopsis misidentify the newspaper titles and claim a bidding contest involving The Sun, while the accessible Guardian report concerns the News of the World. The linked TrumpFile page was reported in prior research as returning HTTP 202 without readable text. The supplied evidence therefore supports a narrow account of the 1968 transaction but gives no documented reason for placing it in a Trump-focused collection. Keep this copy as an exclusion review draft, not as a Trump-linked entry. The source says the stake and management changes were planned; it does not establish that they were completed.
primary.date_basis: The Guardian report is dated 1968-10-25 and says the deal was unfolded 'yesterday'; event date is inferred as 1968-10-24.

In a deal unfolded yesterday to defeat the takeover bid by Pergamon Press, the publishing group headed by Robert Maxwell, MP, the Australian newspaper chain, News Ltd., is to take a 40 per cent stake in the "News of the World." This will be the largest single holding. The chairman of News Ltd., Mr Rupert Murdoch, is to become joint managing director of NoW, with the present chairman, Sir William Carr.

frozen_original.title: Eric Trump Foundation Suspends Charity Events Under AG Scrutiny
frozen_original.synopsis: In June 2017, the Eric Trump Foundation announced it was suspending its annual charity golf tournament fundraising events following scrutiny from the New York attorney general's office over how foundation funds were being spent. The suspension came as investigators were examining whether foundation money had been improperly diverted to Trump business properties. The announcement was a de facto acknowledgment that the foundation's operations could not withstand legal scrutiny. Eric Trump had publicly claimed that his father donated golf course use for free, but documents showed the foundation paid Trump businesses hundreds of thousands of dollars. The foundation ultimately dissolved amid the broader New York AG investigation into Trump family charitable entities.

frozen_original.title: Trump Claims He 'Saved the Economy' with Tariffs Despite Every Major Economist Disagreeing
frozen_original.synopsis: Throughout May 2025, Trump publicly claimed that his tariff policy had 'saved' the American economy despite near-universal condemnation from mainstream economists, business leaders, and international institutions. The IMF, World Bank, and major economic research organizations all projected the tariffs would reduce US GDP and raise consumer prices. Trump selectively cited cherry-picked data while ignoring the broader picture of market turmoil and credit downgrades. The disconnect between Trump's claims and economic reality exemplified his administration's relationship with facts.

primary.title: Internal Draft: Trump’s May 2025 Tariff Claims About the Economy
primary.description_short: Internal draft: the supplied record attributes a “saved the economy” claim to Trump in May 2025, but gives no verified date or transcript.
primary.description_medium: The supplied entry alleges that Trump repeatedly said tariffs had saved the U.S. economy in May 2025 and contrasts the claim with economic forecasts. The packet does not identify a dated statement or transcript for that wording and combines several forecasts, market changes, and credit-rating developments. The absolute phrase “every major economist” is not supported.
primary.description_long: This internal draft preserves the supplied allegation that Trump made repeated May 2025 claims that tariffs had saved the U.S. economy, but the record provides no dated statement or transcript for the quoted wording. The supplied synopsis also groups together statements, forecasts, market moves, credit-rating changes, and predictions about prices and GDP without identifying the source or date for each. A separate official May 30 transcript reviewed for comparison records Trump’s remarks at U.S. Steel’s Irvin Works. In that passage, he said, “We saved the company,” while describing tariffs and the steel producer. That company-specific statement is distinct from the asserted claim about saving the national economy and cannot verify it. This draft therefore attributes the original allegation to the supplied record, removes the absolute assertion that every major economist disagreed, and does not present the quote or economic effects as established. The stored May 1 date is only a month placeholder, not a confirmed statement date. The exact wording, date, and scope of the claimed statement remain unverified, so this copy is not eligible for publication.

frozen_original.title: Trump threatens to strip citizenship from Americans critical of Israel
frozen_original.synopsis: Trump threatened to strip American citizenship from individuals who publicly criticized Israeli government policies, an unconstitutional attempt to punish protected political speech. The threat targeted American citizens exercising their First Amendment rights to criticize foreign policy, and was widely condemned by constitutional scholars who noted that the government cannot strip citizenship as punishment for speech. The threat was seen as part of a broader pattern of using the machinery of government to intimidate critics of US foreign policy toward Israel.

blockers: No accessed source establishes that Trump threatened in March 2025 to revoke U.S. citizenship from American citizens for criticizing Israeli government policy. The reporting located covers different actions: immigration measures against noncitizens, a pro-Israel group's prediction about naturalized citizens, and a later denaturalization policy centered on criminal, national-security, or naturalization-fraud criteria. Those records do not establish the claimed speaker, target, motive, or event date. Treating them as the same event would substitute a different event rather than correct this record.
